prompt: A software company wants to set the price for a new analytics add-on. The candidate's framework: (1) Value the add-on creates for customers; (2) Customers' willingness to pay; (3) Competitor pricing for similar tools; (4) Cost to build and support the add-on. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Missing: the cost to build the add-on
options.feedback: Cost is bucket 4. The flaw is buckets 1 and 2 covering the same question.
Right. Value to the customer and willingness to pay are the same lens. Merge them into customer value and add how the add-on fits the existing price tiers.

options.text: Bucket 3 doesn't matter, since the add-on is new
options.feedback: Customers compare against similar tools, so competitor prices anchor what they will pay.

options.text: It is a generic profitability framework, not a pricing one
options.feedback: Value, competition and cost are the standard pricing lenses here. The issue is the overlap.

explanation: Value created and willingness to pay measure the same thing. Better: customer value, competitor alternatives, cost floor, and fit with the current price tiers (cannibalization).

extras.corrected_framework: Customer value (incl. willingness to pay); competitor alternatives; cost floor; fit with existing tiers and cannibalization
